title: the Marlowe Estate Rising Again
premise: True-crime podcaster Marguerite Eriksen receives two letters about the 1972 deaths at Marlowe Estate: one from a dying man confessing to three 'accidents,' the other from an anonymous writer promising a fourth death before the statute of limitations expires. Her investigation reveals that the sole witness, housemaid Ada Quinn, was declared dead decades ago but may be alive under a stolen identity, protected by the powerful Vane family whose fortune rests on the cover-up. As Marguerite closes in, she discovers her own late mother was Ada's cousin and that the confessing letter-writer is the estate's aging groundskeeper atoning for his silence. In the end, Marguerite finds Ada alive in a coastal convent, exposes the Vanes through a final broadcast rather than the courts, and must choose between the justice the law can offer and the truth that could destroy the innocent along with the guilty.
about_author: Silas Yarrow is the pen name of a former investigative journalist who spent fifteen years covering unsolved cases in the American Northeast before turning to fiction. He lives near the coast with his wife and an archive of coroner's reports he insists are 'research.'

chapters.title: Two Envelopes, One Postmark
chapters.summary: Marguerite Eriksen opens twin letters at her kitchen table: a detailed confession to three deaths at Marlowe Estate, and a taunting note promising a fourth before the statute runs out. POV: Marguerite. Beat: cold dread sharpening into obsession.

chapters.title: The Coldest Case on Record
chapters.summary: Marguerite reviews her files on the 1972 Marlowe deaths—drowning, fire, fall—and the police verdicts of accident. Her producer Bram urges her to drop it. POV: Marguerite. Beat: the pull between career caution and the itch she can't ignore.

chapters.title: What the Ground Remembers
chapters.summary: Marguerite travels to the decaying Marlowe Estate in Vermont, now a crumbling tourist attraction. The groundskeeper, Elias Thorn, watches her too closely. POV: Marguerite. Beat: unease beneath picturesque decay.

chapters.title: A House That Outlived Its Sins
chapters.summary: Elias gives Marguerite a tour heavy with rehearsed answers. She notices a fourth name scratched from the staff ledger: A. Quinn. POV: Marguerite. Beat: first crack in the official story.

chapters.title: Ada Quinn, Deceased
chapters.summary: In the county archives, Marguerite finds Ada Quinn's death certificate dated 1973—yet no body, no grave, no next of kin. POV: Marguerite. Beat: the thrill of the impossible thread.

chapters.title: The Vanes of Marlowe
chapters.summary: Marguerite researches the Vane family, whose philanthropy built half the county. Patriarch Aldous Vane II, ninety-one, still controls local institutions. POV: Marguerite. Beat: the scale of the wall she'll have to climb.

chapters.title: Voices from the Tape
chapters.summary: Marguerite airs a teaser episode; a woman calls in, whispers 'Ask about the boathouse,' and hangs up. POV: Marguerite. Beat: the story waking up and reaching back.

chapters.title: Elias in the Greenhouse
chapters.summary: Elias, tending orchids, tells Marguerite obliquely that some letters are written by men cleaning their souls before death. She realizes he may be her confessor. POV: Marguerite. Beat: suspicion braided with unexpected tenderness.

chapters.title: The Boathouse at Low Water
chapters.summary: At the silted boathouse, Marguerite finds a child's shoe wedged in the pilings—too old to be recent, too preserved to be nothing. POV: Marguerite. Beat: physical evidence making the past undeniable.

chapters.title: Bram's Warning
chapters.summary: Bram arrives unannounced with news: the Vanes' lawyer has sent the network a cease-and-desist. He begs her to kill the season. POV: Bram. Beat: loyalty strained by fear.

chapters.title: A Death Certificate Without a Grave
chapters.summary: Marguerite tracks the doctor who signed Ada's certificate—a retired physician who, before dying last year, left a sealed letter with his attorney. POV: Marguerite. Beat: hope with a price tag.

chapters.title: The Sealed Letter
chapters.summary: The attorney releases the letter for a fee: the doctor admits he falsified Ada's death at Aldous Vane's request, paid to look away from injuries he found 'consistent with violence.' POV: Marguerite. Beat: horror confirmed, proof still thin.

chapters.title: Night Visitor
chapters.summary: Someone searches Marguerite's rental car while she sleeps; her recorder is moved but not taken. They want her to know they can reach her. POV: Marguerite. Beat: fear turning personal.

chapters.title: The Confession, Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Marguerite records herself reading the confession letter and hears what she missed: the writer describes the third death—the fall—from a vantage only a participant could know. POV: Marguerite. Beat: grief for the victims becoming resolve.

chapters.title: Cyrus Vane Comes Down the Hill
chapters.summary: Aldous's grandson Cyrus visits Marguerite, charming and menacing, offering funding for her podcast if she pivots to 'cold cases generally.' POV: Marguerite. Beat: corruption wearing a friendly face.

chapters.title: What My Mother Never Said
chapters.summary: Going through her late mother's boxes, Marguerite finds a photograph of a young woman labeled 'Cousin Ada'—her family is entangled with the witness. POV: Marguerite. Beat: the case becomes blood.

chapters.title: The Second Letter Writer
chapters.summary: Handwriting analysis shows the threatening letter differs from the confession. Two people know everything—one confessing, one protecting. POV: Marguerite. Beat: the shape of the enemy sharpens.

chapters.title: Sister Agnes of St. Brendan's
chapters.summary: Following a pension paper trail, Marguerite reaches a coastal convent where a nun named Sister Agnes entered the order in 1974, age twenty-two. POV: Marguerite. Beat: breath held at the threshold.

chapters.title: The Nun Who Wouldn't Lie
chapters.summary: Sister Agnes denies being Ada—but her hands shake over tea, and she asks one question: 'Is Elias Thorn still alive?' POV: Marguerite. Beat: almost-touching the truth.

chapters.title: Elias Breaks
chapters.summary: Confronted, Elias confesses fully: as a young groundskeeper he helped dispose of evidence after Aldous Vane killed a maid's lover and Ada saw it all. He wrote the confession letter; someone else wrote the threat. POV: Elias. Beat: fifty years of guilt pouring out.

chapters.title: The Fourth Death
chapters.summary: News breaks: the county archivist who handled Ada's file dies in a house fire—ruled accidental. The threat letter was real. POV: Marguerite. Beat: guilt and terror; the clock is no longer theoretical.

chapters.title: Statute of Limitations
chapters.summary: Bram confirms the legal window closes in nineteen days. After that, even a living Ada can be ignored by prosecutors. POV: Bram. Beat: the race made explicit.

chapters.title: Cyrus's Offer, Renewed
chapters.summary: Cyrus returns, colder now, revealing he knows about her mother's connection and implying her family's old debts could ruin her reputation. POV: Marguerite. Beat: power corrupting through leverage, not violence.

chapters.title: The Convent at Night
chapters.summary: Marguerite returns to St. Brendan's and finds Sister Agnes packing a bag—someone warned her to run. Marguerite persuades her to hear Elias's confession recording instead. POV: Marguerite. Beat: trust negotiated in candlelight.

chapters.title: Ada Speaks
chapters.summary: Agnes admits she is Ada Quinn: she saw Aldous Vane kill stablehand Tomas Reyes and fled under the church's protection, declared dead to keep her safe—and silent. POV: Ada. Beat: the witness everyone swears is dead, breathing.

chapters.title: Why She Stayed Dead
chapters.summary: Ada explains: testifying would have meant her death then, and means the convent's exposure now. She has spent fifty years choosing survival over justice. POV: Ada. Beat: love against duty—her vow versus her conscience.

chapters.title: The Missing Hours
chapters.summary: Marguerite reconstructs the night of Tomas's murder using Elias's account, Ada's memory, and the doctored ledgers: three subsequent 'accidents' were witnesses silenced. POV: Marguerite. Beat: the full architecture of the cover-up revealed.

chapters.title: Leak
chapters.summary: Marguerite's hotel room is ransacked; her copies are gone, but she'd already mailed duplicates to Bram. Someone inside her circle is reporting to Cyrus. POV: Marguerite. Beat: paranoia fracturing every alliance.

chapters.title: The Mole
chapters.summary: Marguerite sets a trap with false information through three channels; only one reaches Cyrus. It's her trusted researcher, Dana, paying family medical debt. POV: Marguerite. Beat: betrayal that hurts because it's understandable.

chapters.title: Dana's Choice
chapters.summary: Confronted, Dana breaks down and agrees to feed Cyrus false confirmation that Ada died years ago. POV: Dana. Beat: a small redemption purchased with risk.

chapters.title: Aldous Vane, Awake
chapters.summary: Marguerite requests an interview with the patriarch. He receives her, lucid and cruel, admitting nothing while describing the estate's history as 'necessary pruning.' POV: Marguerite. Beat: face-to-face with corruption incarnate.

chapters.title: The Recording
chapters.summary: Hidden in her coat, Marguerite's recorder catches Aldous referencing 'the girl in the water' unprompted—not a confession, but enough to hang a narrative on. POV: Marguerite. Beat: triumph shadowed by its illegality.

chapters.title: Cyrus Closes the Net
chapters.summary: Cyrus, tipped by a second leak, obtains a court order freezing Marguerite's materials and threatens Bram's job. The lawful paths are sealing shut. POV: Bram. Beat: justice outside the law becomes the only road.

chapters.title: Nineteen Days Become Three
chapters.summary: With the statute expiring Friday, Marguerite, Ada, and Elias agree on a desperate plan: broadcast everything at once, before the Vanes can suppress it. POV: Marguerite. Beat: commitment without guarantee.

chapters.title: The Last Ride to Marlowe
chapters.summary: Driving Ada to the estate to film her testimony on the ground where it happened, Marguerite realizes they're being followed. POV: Marguerite. Beat: dread climbing toward the peak.

chapters.title: Boathouse Reckoning
chapters.summary: Cyrus confronts them at the boathouse; a struggle ends with Elias shielding Ada and taking a blow meant for her. Cyrus flees as storm lights sweep the grounds. POV: Ada. Beat: sacrifice answering fifty years of debt.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: From the estate itself, Marguerite streams the testimony, the confession, the doctor's letter, and Aldous's slip—live, uneditable, everywhere at once. POV: Marguerite. Beat: catharsis; truth detonating beyond anyone's control.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Light
chapters.summary: State police reopen the case; Cyrus is arrested for the archivist's fire and the assault; Aldous, untouchable by statute, faces only history—which proves harsher. POV: Marguerite. Beat: justice partial, but real.

chapters.title: What the Law Couldn't Do
chapters.summary: Ada chooses to testify anyway, not for conviction but so Tomas Reyes gets his name back. Elias, recovering, asks her forgiveness; she gives it slowly. POV: Ada. Beat: grace earned, not granted.

chapters.title: Rising Again
chapters.summary: Months later, Marguerite releases the final episode from the restored estate garden, now a memorial. Ada tends roses where the boathouse stood. Marguerite opens a new envelope—and smiles. POV: Marguerite. Beat: peace, purpose, and the next beginning.
